card: Extracts handling logic for nine P2P message types from PeerManagerImpl::ProcessMessage() into dedicated helper functions in src/net_processing.cpp. The change breaks up a monolithic ~1,000-line message dispatch routine to improve readability and navigation in net_processing. The author cites precedent from merged extractions for pong and addrs messages recommended during review of PR #34588. Nine move-only commits extract the handlers, bounded by a prep commit removing a log prefix and a final commit standardizing formatting.
evidence: PR description notes this continues the pattern established by merged PRs that extracted ProcessPong() (fa5ab022) and ProcessAddrs() (fa55723b), as suggested during review in PR #34588.
problem: PeerManagerImpl::ProcessMessage() is a monolithic function of roughly 1,000 lines handling most P2P message types inline. This makes code navigation, local reasoning, and reviewing changes in net_processing.cpp difficult.

risk.why: Mistakes in extracting P2P message dispatch or control flow could disrupt block, header, or transaction relay or cause peer disconnections.

scope_notes: Large diff across 11 commits, but nine commits are strictly move-only extractions of individual message handlers intended to be reviewed with git --color-moved.
summary: Extracts nine P2P message handlers from PeerManagerImpl::ProcessMessage() in src/net_processing.cpp into dedicated private helper functions. Each handler (getaddr, getdata, getblocks, getheaders, inv, sendtxrcncl, tx, cmpctblock, and version) is moved in an isolated commit to facilitate move-only review. A preparatory commit removes a redundant __func__ prefix from a debug log, and a trailing cleanup commit normalizes formatting and local control flow.
